meta.title: O-RADS US Classification
meta.subtitle: Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System · ACR v2022
meta.disclaimer: Educational material only. Does not replace the official ACR Guidance app or specialist clinical judgment.
meta.source: American College of Radiology (ACR). O-RADS US Risk Stratification and Management System, version 2022.

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: O-RADS US was developed by the American College of Radiology (ACR) as a standardized system to describe and stratify malignancy risk of ovarian and adnexal lesions on ultrasound. Version v2022 continues the RADS family (BI-RADS, LI-RADS, LU-RADS, etc.) within the ACR Guidance Reporting and Data Systems module.
The main goals are unified terminology, reduced interobserver variability, and clear management: surveillance, specialist referral, or gynecologic oncology.

sections.title: 1.1. ACR Guidance structure
paragraphs: The ACR Guidance app consolidates clinical decision support:
bullets: Reporting and Data Systems (RADS) — including O-RADS US;
Incidental Findings (IF) — management of incidental findings.

sections.title: 2. Assessment principles
paragraphs: The O-RADS US algorithm is a sequential dichotomous tree: localization → content → wall/septal morphology → solid component → IOTA color score. In ACR Guidance this appears as: Ovarian/Adnexal or Extraovarian → Lesion → morphologic detail.

sections.title: 2.1. Localization
paragraphs: First step: ovarian vs extraovarian (paraovarian cyst, hydrosalpinx, peritoneal inclusion cyst, etc.). Extraovarian lesions follow a separate risk branch.

sections.title: 2.2. Lesion content
paragraphs: For ovarian lesions: simple (anechoic, no internal echoes) vs non-simple (septa, solid component, heterogeneous content). Color Doppler assesses wall, septal, and solid vascularity.

sections.title: 3. Lesion morphology
paragraphs: Classification by inner wall and septa: simple vs non-simple.

sections.title: 3.1. Simple cysts
paragraphs: Unilocular, anechoic, smooth wall, no solid component and no internal flow on Doppler. In premenopause, often O-RADS 2 (with size/menopause thresholds applied in the calculator).

sections.title: 3.2. Non-simple cysts
paragraphs: Internal echoes (e.g. hemorrhagic content) and/or incomplete septation — thin septa not reaching the opposite wall.

sections.title: 3.3. Wall and septa
paragraphs: For non-simple cysts: smooth vs irregular inner wall/septum. Critical nodular thickness threshold: <3 mm vs ≥3 mm (solid component / papillary projection).

sections.title: 4. Solid component and Doppler
paragraphs: A solid component raises risk category. Assess contour (smooth/irregular), echogenicity, and IOTA color score (1–4) from no flow to marked vascularity.

sections.title: 5. O-RADS categories 0–5
paragraphs: The algorithm yields a risk category with malignancy risk (ROM) range and management recommendation.

sections.title: 5.1. Clinical significance
paragraphs: O-RADS 1–2 — usually no oncologic work-up: physiology, simple cyst, classic benign (typical dermoid, endometrioma, hemorrhagic cyst).
O-RADS 3 — low risk: short-interval follow-up or gynecology (thin septa without marked flow).
O-RADS 4 — intermediate risk: solid component with measurable flow → gynecologic oncology.
O-RADS 5 — high risk (≥50%): multilocular-solid with papillary projections, marked irregular vascularity, ascites/peritoneal nodules.

sections.title: 6. Conclusion
paragraphs: O-RADS US enables structured reporting and quantitative risk assessment. The stepwise algorithm from localization through Doppler improves reproducibility across operators and sites.
An interactive calculator with reference sonograms supports daily practice. In Sonogyn Pro: O-RADS US v2022 Wizard plus this educational guide.
